**Triage** — graded `p2`, `documentation`, `pm:queue`, routed **`domain:spec`**. (Applied and read back first.)

## Routing, because the symptom and the fix are in different lanes

The damage is customer-visible in `skills/objectstack-i18n/references/_index.md`, which reads as `domain:skills`. The **fix** is in `packages/spec/scripts/build-skill-references.ts`, and the lane table names `packages/spec/scripts/**` for `domain:spec` explicitly. Anchoring rule: the lane follows where the repair lands.

That also matches the siblings — **#14462 is already `documentation` / `priority:p2` / `pm:queue` / `domain:spec`** — so all three of this group now sit in one lane, which is what you asked for when you said they are worth triaging as one group. `p2` is the siblings' grade too, and this card carries the same cost, so it takes the same number rather than a lower one for being newer.

## Re-measured at `origin/main` `c616c2c` — everything confirmed

`SKILL_MAP['objectstack-i18n']` is exactly the two entries you quote, so your central point stands: **the core list is right and the defect is downstream of it.**

`_index.md`'s "Transitive dependencies" section lists exactly **7** pointers, matching your table item for item:

```
data/field-value.zod.ts · data/field.zod.ts · data/filter.zod.ts ·
kernel/metadata-protection.zod.ts · shared/expression.zod.ts ·
shared/identifiers.zod.ts · shared/suggestions.zod.ts
```

## Why the reachability argument is the load-bearing part

`FieldTranslationSchema` is four optional strings and a string map, and a bundle addresses everything **by name string** — so no filter, expression, field value or protection rule is reachable from an authorable bundle, and the object/field/view names are map keys validated by the lint pass rather than by importing those schemas. That is a *semantic* claim about the authorable face, not a count, and it is what distinguishes this from an over-eager import graph that happens to be noisy. The closure is following edges that exist for reasons the authorable face never surfaces.

⭐ Note the largest of the five, `data/filter.zod.ts`, is the **Unified Query DSL** — a different skill's whole subject, shipped into every i18n session with an instruction to `Read` it.

## Scope

⛔ **Do not hand-edit `_index.md`.** It is generator-owned and the next `gen:skill-refs` undoes it. You said this; I am making it binding.

Read #14462 and #14466 first, as you advise. Your own framing of the choice is the right one and I am adopting it as the scope note rather than ruling it: a per-package transitive allowlist/denylist beside `SKILL_MAP` fixes this card only; a reachability rule ("only follow imports the package's authorable face can actually reach") generalises to all three. ⭐ The second is the better shape *if it can be made precise* — but "reachable from the authorable face" is exactly the semantic judgement you had to make by hand above, and a generator cannot infer it from import edges alone. Whoever takes this should decide that feasibility question **first** and say so in the PR body, because it determines whether this is one fix or three.

⛔ Do not fold in #14315. That flight was shrink-only inside `skills/objectstack-i18n/` and deferred this by its own scope; deferring it was correct.

Implemented in draft PR #15268 (family branch `claude/issue-14462-skill-map-reconciliation`; commit `735fc9d7` is this card's). The feasibility question is answered first and in the PR body: **a general reachability rule is unbuildable from this input**, and the required outcome is the proof — `shared/identifiers.zod.ts` must be kept although nothing imports it, while `kernel/metadata-protection.zod.ts` must go although it is a first-class direct import of `system/translation.zod.ts`; no predicate over the import graph orders those two that way. So route 2: a per-package transitive **allowlist** beside `SKILL_MAP`, opt-in, with a guard that refuses a wrong package name, an unreachable file, a file already in core, or a repeat. Criterion met: all five named pointers gone, `shared/identifiers.zod.ts` kept, `data/field.zod.ts` **kept** (the call left to the implementer — `FieldTranslationSchema.options` is keyed by select-option value and `SelectOptionSchema` is the declaration those keys must match). One premise drift worth recording: the index carried **eight** transitive pointers at this base, not the seven measured on the card — `shared/value-domain.zod.ts` joined later through a new import edge several files away, which is also why the constraint is an allowlist and not a denylist.
